title: Anti-rug trigger dedupe, retry and circuit-breaker counting

options.name: Keep current behaviour: every matching log dispatch is its own exit attempt and its own breaker count; a refused or failed escape is not retried
options.risk: One rug can trip the chain breaker and suppress every later anti-rug exit on the chain (AUD-ANTIRUG-003); a refused or failed escape is lost (AUD-ANTIRUG-004).

options.name: One in-flight anti-rug dispatch per position; an unsafe verdict stays pending and is retried each block until a successful exit or a genuine close
options.behavior_impact: Duplicate logs no longer start duplicate attempts; a failed escape is retried.
options.risk: A retry loop on a position that cannot be sold (honeypot, no route) burns gas each block unless bounded.

options.name: dedupe-and-retry, and count the breaker once per position (or per rug event) instead of per dispatch
options.behavior_impact: The breaker trips on several positions misfiring, not on one rug.
options.risk: A detector misfiring repeatedly on one position is no longer caught by the breaker; needs its own bound.

recommendation: dedupe-retry-count-per-position with a bounded retry, decided after the Phase 23 fork replay counts the logs of a complete removal.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract). This card covers S1 capital findings, which cannot rest on the default: until it is decided and fixed it blocks the live re-entry gate.
behavior_impact: Decides how many exit attempts and breaker counts one rug produces.
needed_by: Phase 24 discussion (capital fixes, after the Phase 23 real-path proof)
